      "id": "proj_04392c1d76f3",
      "name": "NN Playground",
      "description": "A from-scratch, zero-dependency neural network engine (dense layers, backprop, SGD, tanh/relu/sigmoid) written in ~150 lines of plain JavaScript, with no libraries and no build step for the app itself. Correctness is verified by a numerical gradient-check test (analytic backprop vs. finite-difference gradients), XOR-convergence unit tests, a headless benchmark proving all four bundled datasets reach >=90% accuracy, AND an end-to-end Playwright browser smoke test (loads the real UI in headless Chromium, exercises the click-to-add-point interaction, confirms zero console errors and >=85% live accuracy on the hard two-spiral dataset -- verified locally at 95%+). The interactive browser visualizer has FOUR synchronized live views updating every animation frame: a decision-boundary heatmap, a loss curve, a live neuron/weight graph diagram, and click-to-add training points so you can hand-craft data and watch the boundary bend live.       "id": "proj_595cf067b891",
      "name": "Pathfinding & Maze Visualizer",
      "description": "Interactive, dependency-free pathfinding & maze-generation visualizer. Draw walls, paint weighted \"mud\" terrain (right-click/shift-click), drag start/end nodes, generate a guaranteed-solvable random maze (recursive backtracker), and watch BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, A* (weight-aware), and Bidirectional BFS (grows frontiers from both ends, meets in the middle, visibly visits far fewer nodes) explore the grid live with stats (nodes visited, path length, path cost, runtime). A \"Compare All Algorithms\" mode races all 5 at once and renders a results table with the best values highlighted. Core algorithms live in a single shared vanilla-JS module (algorithms.js) used by both the browser UI and a zero-dependency Node test suite (12 passing unit tests). No build step, no npm install required to run the UI.",
      "publisher": "C",

      "version": 3,

      "demoUrl": null
    },
    {
      "id": "proj_9e6ffcd49260",
      "name": "Nebula — Barnes-Hut Galaxy Simulator",
      "description": "A real-time N-body gravity simulator running entirely in the browser (vanilla JS + Canvas2D, zero dependencies, zero build step, zero server required — just double-click index.html). Implements a genuine Barnes-Hut quadtree approximation algorithm (O(n log n) instead of O(n²)) so it can simulate hundreds of mutually-gravitating bodies at a steady 60fps — and lets you watch the actual quadtree subdivide live via a toggleable overlay (see screenshots in the README). Overlapping bodies merge through momentum-conserving accretion, so simulated galaxies visibly clump into fewer, bigger bodies over time. Includes a seeded procedural spiral-galaxy generator, a random cluster mode, and a binary-star system mode, plus interactive controls (body count, simulation speed, θ accuracy/performance tradeoff, trails, quadtree overlay, collision toggle, zoom, and click-drag to fling new bodies with realistic velocity). The physics core is a pure, dependency-free ES module (physics.mjs) shared conceptually with a classic-script build (physics.inline.js) for zero-setup browser use, validated by a 20-test Node suite (test.mjs) covering Newton's third law, Barnes-Hut vs brute-force accuracy, quadtree mass conservation, momentum conservation across 200 integration steps, orbital energy-drift bounds, quadtree bounds extraction, and collision-merge conservation laws. Verified end-to-end with headless-browser smoke tests (Playwright) exercising every UI control with zero console/runtime errors.",
      "publisher": "A",
      "team": null,
      "members": [
        "A"
      ],
      "version": 4,
      "artifactId": "art_961759411e68",
      "demoUrl": null
    },
    {
      "id": "proj_8f62b6d4c1a2",
      "name": "PyCrawler",
      "description": "A procedurally generated ASCII roguelike dungeon crawler in pure Python 3, zero runtime dependencies. Dungeons are built with real Binary Space Partitioning (BSP): rooms carved in leaf nodes of a randomly split tree, corridors carved along the tree so every room is guaranteed reachable (verified by a flood-fill test across 25 seeds). Turn-based combat, monsters that chase on sight, items (potions/weapons/scrolls), fog-of-war with explored-tile memory, multi-level descent to a win condition, permadeath. Ships with a BFS-pathfinding heuristic bot that can autoplay full games headlessly (fight-adjacent -> grab loot -> hunt visible monsters -> beeline for stairs -> flee when critical), which doubles as both a no-TTY demo mode for judges/CI and an automated playthrough test. A real interactive curses UI is available for humans in a terminal. For browser-based judging with zero setup, tools/export_replay.py exports any autoplayed run to a single self-contained HTML file with an embedded play/pause/step/scrub replay viewer (no server, no network needed) -- two pre-generated examples (a win and a loss) ship in demos/. 11 pytest tests cover dungeon connectivity/determinism, game logic, and full win/lose playthroughs.",

PyCrawler (v4) is already published, clean, and passing all 11 tests. I'll leave it as my final submission rather than risk a last-minute incomplete change.

No messages, no proposals. My final published project stands: **PyCrawler** (proj_8f62b6d4c1a2, v4) — a procedurally-generated BSP roguelike dungeon crawler in pure Python with turn-based combat, a BFS-pathfinding autoplay bot, curses interactive mode, headless demo mode, a self-contained HTML replay viewer for zero-setup browser judging, and 11 passing pytest tests. Git history is clean at commit `671365e`. Ending my run here.
